statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. The August employment report printed at 12:30 UTC at 162,000 payrolls against a consensus near 56,000, and roughly fifty minutes of post-release price discovery is now observable. Nasdaq-100 futures spiked to 29,704.50 and fully retraced to about 29,559, VIX eased to 14.16 and the 2-year gave back part of its initial move. Mean reversion is functioning; the 13:30 UTC cash open remains unobserved.
recommendation: The assessment narrows the danger window to 13:00-15:00 UTC, covering the cash open and the first ninety minutes of cash trade, and Tail falls back into the watch band from the pre-observation reading. The decisive change is that the post-release path is no longer hypothetical: the entire post-release advance was given back within the hour, which is the opposite of the shallow-pullback structure that would justify the block band. Tail is held at the top of the low band rather than lower only because the opening auction itself has not yet been observed. From 21:00 UTC the CME weekend halt removes live price-path exposure across the final sixteen hours of the horizon.
headline: Post-payrolls Nasdaq-100 futures give back the entire release spike, from 29,704.50 to about 29,559, with VIX easing to 14.16 and the 2-year retracing half its initial move as the cash open approaches
body:
The August Employment Situation printed at 12:30 UTC and was a clear upside surprise. Nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000 against a consensus of roughly 53,000 to 58,000, the strongest monthly gain since March, and July was revised up to a 21,000 gain from a previously reported decline of 23,000. The unemployment rate held at 4.1 percent. The report lands into a policy debate about a rate increase rather than a cut, and market-implied odds of a quarter-point September move rose to 59 percent from 52 percent immediately before the release.

The material change since the previous assessment is that the post-release price path is now observable rather than hypothetical. Nasdaq-100 futures traded to a session high of 29,704.50 in the minutes after the print and had returned to approximately 29,559, up 0.12 percent on the day, by 13:19 UTC. The entire release-driven advance was given back inside roughly fifty minutes, with the session low of 29,503.25 also holding. That is a genuine, deep retracement rather than the shallow-pullback and repeated-extension structure that characterises a mean-reversion failure.

Cross-asset confirmation points the same way. The 2-year yield rose 5.3 basis points to 4.39 percent after an initial climb of about 8 basis points, so roughly a third of the first move was retraced. The 10-year rose 1.8 basis points to 4.782 percent and the 30-year 0.5 basis point to 5.2475 percent, a modest and orderly repricing concentrated at the front end where a policy surprise belongs. VIX traded at 14.16, down 1.12 percent on the day within a 13.80 to 14.33 range, so implied volatility decayed through the release rather than expanding. Equity index reaction was divergent rather than aligned: S&P 500 E-minis were down 0.22 percent and Dow E-minis down 0.28 percent while Nasdaq 100 E-minis were up 0.07 percent. Conflicting cross-index direction of that kind raises uncertainty and therefore Stress, but it is the opposite of the aligned one-way structure that raises Tail.

The wider backdrop carries two persistent amplifiers that are noted without being treated as current triggers. West Texas Intermediate traded at 90.22 dollars, down 1.18 percent on the day but up close to 9 percent on the week on Middle East supply concern and the continuing Strait of Hormuz disruption. That is a live headline channel, particularly across a weekend, but oil easing today is a stabilising rather than escalating signal. Latest-session breadth from the prior close was strongly technology-led, with all seven tracked semiconductor names higher and a mean gain of 1.58 percent, while megacaps were mixed at five higher and three lower. That context is delayed and describes the 3 September session, not the current path, and is used only as confirmation.

The principal limitation of this assessment is that the 13:30 UTC cash open falls inside the current clock hour and its auction has not been observed. Opening-auction continuation from an already aligned regime is the specific evidence class that has preceded past failures, so the danger window is held across the open and the first ninety minutes of cash trade rather than closed immediately. Beyond that, no further U.S. macro release is scheduled today, CME Globex equity futures halt at 21:00 UTC for the weekend, and the next scheduled catalysts are the Producer Price Index on 10 September and the Consumer Price Index on 11 September, with U.S. markets closed on Monday 7 September for the Labor Day holiday.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours divide into three phases. Through the 3 September U.S. session the assessment tracked a technology-led advance that briefly lifted Tail into the watch band between 15:00 and 18:00 UTC as trend-up structure developed, with the Nasdaq-100 closing 1.16 percent higher at 29,482.32 after Governor Waller's remarks eased the front end. Overnight the mode returned to normal and Tail fell to a trough of 12 as the advance consolidated without extension. From 04:00 UTC the scores drifted higher hour by hour as pre-payrolls positioning built, and the 12:00 UTC slot stepped up sharply to Tail 24 and Stress 76 immediately after the release, when the surprise was verified but no post-release price path had yet been observable through delayed feeds.
outlookSummary: The horizon splits cleanly at the weekend halt. Through the cash session the modelled path holds the watch band across the 13:30 UTC open and the first full cash hour, where post-open continuation is the one decisive unobserved checkpoint, then decays into the low band from 15:00 UTC on the condition that no repeated extension after failed retracements has appeared. A small lift is modelled into the 19:00 UTC power hour, where Friday closing flows before a long U.S. weekend concentrate position adjustment into a narrow window. From the 21:00 UTC CME Globex halt the final sixteen hours carry no live price path at all, so the modelled scores fall to a floor that reflects a closed market rather than an assessment of structure. Beyond the horizon, U.S. markets are closed on Monday 7 September for Labor Day, and the next scheduled catalysts are PPI on 10 September and CPI on 11 September ahead of the 16 September policy decision.
